catalog.name: Vegetation and Land Surface
catalog.description: Vegetation and land surface datasets from NASA Earth observation missions, including canopy characteristics from GEDI and vegetation indices from MODIS.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: Data provided by NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS). GEDI mission team at NASA Goddard Space Flight Center. MODIS mission team. Contact: earthdata-support@nasa.gov

info.name: License
info.content: NASA data is generally available for public use. Please check individual dataset licenses and cite appropriately.

info.name: Coverage
info.content: Global coverage with various temporal and spatial resolutions. GEDI provides discrete lidar measurements between 51.6°N and 51.6°S.

members.name: GEDI Canopy Characteristics
members.description: Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) provides high-resolution measurements of forest canopy height, biomass, and structure using spaceborne lidar technology.

members.name: GEDI Aboveground Biomass Density
members.description: GEDI-derived estimates of aboveground biomass density in forested ecosystems, providing crucial data for carbon cycle studies.

info.name: Background
info.content: GEDI uses advanced lidar technology from the International Space Station to measure forest canopy height and structure, which is then used to estimate aboveground biomass density - a key parameter for carbon storage assessment.

info.name: Measurement Unit
info.content: Megagrams of carbon per hectare (Mg C/ha)

info.name: Spatial Coverage
info.content: 51.6°N to 51.6°S latitude, covering most forested regions globally

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: 2019 to present

info.name: Applications
info.content: Carbon cycle research, forest management, REDD+ initiatives, climate change mitigation

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA GEDI mission team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, University of Maryland

members.name: GEDI Canopy Height Mean
members.description: Mean canopy height measurements from GEDI lidar, providing detailed information about forest vertical structure.

info.name: Background
info.content: GEDI measures the vertical structure of forests by sending laser pulses to Earth and analyzing the returned signals. Canopy height is a fundamental parameter for ecosystem studies and biodiversity assessment.

info.name: Measurement Unit
info.content: Meters above ground

info.name: Vertical Resolution
info.content: Sub-meter precision in height measurements

info.name: Applications
info.content: Forest inventory, habitat mapping, biodiversity studies, forest health monitoring

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA GEDI mission team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, University of Maryland

members.name: GEDI Canopy Height Standard Deviation
members.description: Standard deviation of canopy height measurements from GEDI, indicating forest structural complexity and heterogeneity.

info.name: Background
info.content: The standard deviation of canopy height provides insights into forest structural complexity - higher values indicate more heterogeneous canopy structure, often associated with older or more diverse forests.

info.name: Interpretation
info.content: Low values: uniform canopy (plantations, young forests). High values: complex structure (old-growth, mixed forests)

info.name: Applications
info.content: Forest structural assessment, biodiversity indicators, forest management planning

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA GEDI mission team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, University of Maryland

members.name: GEDI Number of Samples
members.description: Number of GEDI lidar samples per grid cell, indicating data density and measurement confidence.

info.name: Background
info.content: This layer shows the number of individual GEDI measurements within each grid cell, providing information about data density and statistical confidence of derived parameters.

info.name: Data Quality
info.content: Higher sample numbers generally indicate more reliable statistics and better spatial representation

info.name: Applications
info.content: Data quality assessment, uncertainty analysis, research planning

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA GEDI mission team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, University of Maryland

members.name: Land Surface Temperature
members.description: Land surface temperature measurements providing insights into surface energy balance, urban heat islands, and vegetation stress.

members.name: AIRS Surface Skin Temperature (Day) - Monthly
members.description: Daytime surface skin temperature from AIRS, representing the interface temperature between land surface and atmosphere.

info.name: Background
info.content: Surface skin temperature is the temperature of the Earth's surface as measured by thermal infrared sensors. It differs from air temperature and is crucial for energy balance studies.

info.name: Temporal Sampling
info.content: Daytime observations (~1:30 PM local time)

info.name: Applications
info.content: Urban heat island studies, drought monitoring, land surface modeling, energy balance research

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA AIRS mission team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center

members.name: AIRS Surface Skin Temperature (Night) - Monthly
members.description: Nighttime surface skin temperature from AIRS, providing complementary data to daytime observations for diurnal cycle analysis.

info.name: Background
info.content: Nighttime surface skin temperature measurements help understand diurnal temperature cycles and surface cooling processes.

info.name: Temporal Sampling
info.content: Nighttime observations (~1:30 AM local time)

info.name: Applications
info.content: Diurnal cycle studies, surface cooling analysis, thermal inertia research

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA AIRS mission team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
